# Auto-generated pattern: declare shared members on the generic base classes
# so `Score`/`Track`/... (the public generic types) resolve them, instead of
# the members living only on the concrete <X>Tick/<X>Quarter/<X>Second leaves.

symusic\.core\.Score$:
    class Score(Generic[TimeUnitT]):
        """
        Score[TimeUnitT](tpq: int = 480)
        Container for a full MIDI score consisting of named tracks, tempo/key/time metadata, and helper
        methods for serialization and transformations. This variant stores timestamps as floating-point seconds aligned with the tempo map.
        Parameters
        ----------
        tpq:
            Reference ticks-per-quarter retained for precise conversion back to tick or beat timelines.
        Note
        ----
        - Time values are 32-bit floats measured in seconds.
        - Optimized for audio alignment, wall-clock automation, or duration-based editing
        - Score objects expose Pythonic semantics such as slicing, repr/eq, and pickling.
        - ``tpq`` travels with the tempo map so conversions remain lossless.
        Examples
        --------
        .. code-block:: python
            from symusic import Score[TimeUnitT]
            score = Score[TimeUnitT](960)
            dump_path = "example.mid"
            score.dump_midi(dump_path)
        """
        @overload
        def __init__(self, tpq: int, /) -> None:
            """Create an empty score with the provided ticks-per-quarter resolution."""
        @overload
        def __init__(self, other: Score[TimeUnitT], /) -> None:
            """Clone another score, deep-copying its tracks and events."""
        @overload
        def __init__(self, path: pathlib.Path, /) -> None:
            """
            Load a MIDI file from disk into a score. Accepts strings or ``pathlib.Path`` objects pointing to a
            ``.mid``/``.midi`` file.
            """
        def copy(self, deep: bool = True, /) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """Return a shallow or deep copy depending on *deep*."""
        def __copy__(self, /) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """Return a shallow copy of the score."""
        def __deepcopy__(self, memo: object, _nil: object, /) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """Create a deep copy suitable for Python's copy module."""
        def __repr__(self, /) -> str:
            """Generate a textual summary of the score."""
        @overload
        def __eq__(self, other: Score[TimeUnitT], /) -> bool:
            """Scores compare equal when their handles or contents match."""
        @overload
        def __eq__(self, other: object, /) -> bool: ...
        @overload
        def __ne__(self, other: Score[TimeUnitT], /) -> bool:
            """Scores compare equal when their handles or contents match."""
        @overload
        def __ne__(self, other: object, /) -> bool: ...
        def __getstate__(self, /) -> bytes:
            """Serialize the score into ZPP bytes for pickling."""
        def __setstate__(self, state: bytes, /) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """Rehydrate the score from serialized ZPP bytes."""
        @staticmethod
        def from_file(path: str | os.PathLike, format: str | None = None, sanitize_data: bool = False) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Read a score from disk by auto-detecting a MIDI or ABC file. Use ``format`` (``"midi"`` or
            ``"abc"``) when the extension is ambiguous.
            """
        @staticmethod
        def from_midi(data: bytes, sanitize_data: bool = False) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Parse raw MIDI bytes into a score. When ``sanitize_data`` is ``True``, controller/pitch values are
            clamped into the MIDI-safe range.
            """
        @staticmethod
        def from_abc(abc: str) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Parse an ABC notation string into a score. Requires the ``SYMUSIC_ABC2MIDI`` environment variable
            to point to the abc2midi executable.
            """
        def dump_midi(self, path: str | os.PathLike) -> None:
            """
            Write the score to a MIDI file using the current ticks-per-quarter resolution.
            """
        def dumps_midi(self) -> bytes:
            """Serialize the score into MIDI bytes for in-memory workflows."""
        def dump_abc(self, path: str | os.PathLike, warn: bool = False) -> None:
            """
            Dump the score to an ABC file via midi2abc. Temporary MIDI files are cleaned up automatically.
            """
        def dumps_abc(self, warn: bool = False) -> str:
            """
            Return the score as an ABC notation string. Set *warn* to ``False`` to silence stderr.
            """
        def get_beats(self, start_time: float = 0.0) -> NDArray[numpy.float32]:
            """
            Return beat locations as a NumPy array in the score's current time unit. Compound meters follow the
            PrettyMIDI heuristic of grouping every three denominator notes into one beat.
            """
        def get_downbeats(self, start_time: float = 0.0) -> NDArray[numpy.float32]:
            """
            Return downbeat locations as a NumPy array in the score's current time unit. When no time
            signature is available at *start_time*, a 4/4 sentinel is assumed.
            """
        @property
        def ticks_per_quarter(self) -> int:
            """Ticks per quarter note"""
        @ticks_per_quarter.setter
        def ticks_per_quarter(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...
        @property
        def tpq(self) -> int:
            """Alias of ticks_per_quarter"""
        @tpq.setter
        def tpq(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...
        @property
        def tracks(self) -> list[Track[TimeUnitT]]:

        @tracks.setter
        def tracks(self, arg: list[Track[TimeUnitT]], /) -> None: ...
        @property
        def time_signatures(self) -> list[TimeSignature[TimeUnitT]]:

        def tempos(self) -> list[Tempo[TimeUnitT]]:
            """List of tempo events"""
        @tempos.setter
        def tempos(self, arg: list[Tempo[TimeUnitT]], /) -> None: ...
        @property
        def markers(self) -> list[TextMeta[TimeUnitT]]:
            """List of text/marker events"""
        @markers.setter
        def markers(self, arg: list[TextMeta[TimeUnitT]], /) -> None: ...
        @property
        def ttype(self) -> TimeUnitT:
            """Time unit type — Tick/Quarter/TimeUnitT"""
        def __use_count(self) -> int:
            """
            Return the reference count of the shared score pointer for debugging aliasing.
            """
        def to(self, ttype: object, min_dur: object | None = None) -> object:
            """
            Convert the score to another time unit (Tick, Quarter, TimeUnitT). ``ttype`` may be a class object or
            ``"tick"/"quarter"/"second"``. ``min_dur`` snaps durations when downsampling.
            """
        def resample(self, tpq: int, min_dur: float | None = None) -> ScoreTick:
            """
            Resample the score to a new ticks-per-quarter resolution. ``min_dur`` controls rounding behaviour
            when reducing resolution.
            """
        def sort(self, reverse: bool = False, inplace: bool = True) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Sort tracks chronologically. When *inplace* is False the operation occurs on a copy.
            """
        def clip(self, start: float, end: float, clip_end: bool = False, inplace: bool = False) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Clip the score to [start, end). When *inplace* is False returns a new score.
            """
        def shift_time(self, offset: float, inplace: bool = False) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Shift every event timestamp by *offset*. When *inplace* is False operate on a copy.
            """
        def shift_pitch(self, offset: int, inplace: bool = False) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Shift every note by *offset* semitones. When *inplace* is False operate on a copy.
            """
        def shift_velocity(self, offset: int, inplace: bool = False) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Shift every note velocity by *offset*. When *inplace* is False operate on a copy.
            """
        def start(self) -> float:
            """Return the earliest timestamp across all tracks."""
        def end(self) -> float:
            """Return the exclusive end timestamp across all tracks."""
        def note_num(self) -> int:
            """Return the total number of notes across all tracks."""
        def empty(self) -> bool:
            """Return True when the score contains no notes."""
        def adjust_time(self, original_times: Sequence[float], new_times: Sequence[float], inplace: bool = False) -> Score[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Remap timestamps across all tracks using aligned original/new time arrays. Operates in place unless specified.
            """

    class Track(Generic[TimeUnitT]):
        r"""
        Track[TimeUnitT](name: str = "", program: int = 0, is_drum: bool = False)
        ====================================================================
        Container for per-channel events (notes, controllers, pedals, pitch bends, metadata) tied to a MIDI
        program. Tracks emulate Python lists: copy, compare, repr, and pickling propagate through the shared
        pointer. This variant stores timestamps as floating-point seconds aligned with the tempo map.
        Parameters
        ----------
        name:
            Human-friendly identifier used when printing or exporting.
        program:
            MIDI program number (0-127). Defaults to acoustic grand piano.
        is_drum:
            Flag drum/percussion channels. Useful when writing to SMF channel 10.
        Note
        ----
        - Time values are 32-bit floats measured in seconds.
        - Optimized for audio alignment, wall-clock automation, or duration-based editing
        - Durations and controller timestamps share the same second units
        Examples
        --------
        .. code-block:: python
            from symusic import Track[TimeUnitT], Note[TimeUnitT]
            track = Track[TimeUnitT](name=\"Piano\")
            track.notes.append(Note[TimeUnitT](0, 120, 60, 90))
        """
        @overload
        def __init__(self, /) -> None:
            """Create an empty track bound to the current time unit."""
        @overload
        def __init__(self, name: str = '', program: int = 0, is_drum: bool = False, /) -> None:

    class Note(Generic[TimeUnitT]):
        """
        Note[TimeUnitT](time: float, duration: float, pitch: int, velocity: int = 0)
        Pitched event anchored to a second timestamp with editable duration and velocity.
        - Time values are 32-bit floats measured in seconds.
        - Optimized for audio alignment, wall-clock automation, or duration-based editing
        - Durations use the same second units
        """
        @overload
        def __init__(self, other: Note[TimeUnitT], /) -> None:
            """Copy an existing event into this shared pointer wrapper."""
        @overload
        def __init__(self, time: float, duration: float, pitch: int, velocity: int = 0) -> None:
            """Create a note event from timing, duration, pitch, and velocity values."""
        @property
        def time(self, /) -> float:
            """Event timestamp in chosen time unit"""
        @time.setter
        def time(self, value: float, /) -> None: ...
        @property
        def ttype(self, /) -> TimeUnitT:
            """Time unit type — Tick/Quarter/TimeUnitT"""
        def shift_time(self, offset: float, inplace: bool = False) -> Note[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Shift the event's timestamp by *offset*. When *inplace* is False a cloned event is returned.
            """
        def copy(self, deep: bool = True, /) -> Note[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Return a shallow or deep copy depending on *deep*. Deep copies duplicate underlying storage.
            """
        def __copy__(self, /) -> Note[TimeUnitT]:
            """Return a shallow copy of the event."""
        def __deepcopy__(self, memo: object, _nil: object, /) -> Note[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Create a deep copy of the event suitable for Python's copy module helpers.
            """

            """Serialize the event into its human-friendly textual form."""
        @overload
        def __eq__(self, other: Note[TimeUnitT], /) -> bool:
            """
            Events compare equal when they refer to the same pointer or when their values match.
            """
        @overload
        def __eq__(self, other: object, /) -> bool: ...
        @overload
        def __ne__(self, other: Note[TimeUnitT], /) -> bool:
            """Events compare not-equal when their value representation differs."""

            """Events compare not-equal when their value representation differs."""

symusic\.core\.TimeSignature$:
    class TimeSignature(Generic[TimeUnitT]):
        """
        TimeSignature[TimeUnitT](time: float, numerator: int, denominator: int)
        Meter change storing beats-per-bar and subdivision (e.g., ``3/4``) on the second timeline. The denominator must be a power of two because it represents note lengths.
        - Time values are 32-bit floats measured in seconds.
        - Optimized for audio alignment, wall-clock automation, or duration-based editing
        """
        @overload
        def __init__(self, other: TimeSignature[TimeUnitT], /) -> None:
            """Copy an existing event into this shared pointer wrapper."""
        @overload
        def __init__(self, time: float, numerator: int, denominator: int) -> None:
            """
            Create a time signature event with *time*, *numerator*, and *denominator*.
            """
        @property
        def time(self, /) -> float:
            """Event timestamp in chosen time unit"""
        @time.setter
        def time(self, value: float, /) -> None: ...
        @property
        def ttype(self, /) -> TimeUnitT:
            """Time unit type — Tick/Quarter/TimeUnitT"""
        def shift_time(self, offset: float, inplace: bool = False) -> TimeSignature[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Shift the event's timestamp by *offset*. When *inplace* is False a cloned event is returned.
            """
        def copy(self, deep: bool = True, /) -> TimeSignature[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Return a shallow or deep copy depending on *deep*. Deep copies duplicate underlying storage.
            """
        def __copy__(self, /) -> TimeSignature[TimeUnitT]:
            """Return a shallow copy of the event."""
        def __deepcopy__(self, memo: object, _nil: object, /) -> TimeSignature[TimeUnitT]:
            """
            Create a deep copy of the event suitable for Python's copy module helpers.
            """
        def __repr__(self, /) -> str:
            """Serialize the event into its human-friendly textual form."""
        @overload
        def __eq__(self, other: TimeSignature[TimeUnitT], /) -> bool:
            """
            Events compare equal when they refer to the same pointer or when their values match.
            """
        @overload
        def __eq__(self, other: object, /) -> bool: ...
        @overload
        def __ne__(self, other: TimeSignature[TimeUnitT], /) -> bool:
            """Events compare not-equal when their value representation differs."""
        @overload
        def __ne__(self, other: object, /) -> bool:
            """Events compare not-equal when their value representation differs."""
        @overload
        def __ne__(self, arg: TimeSignature[TimeUnitT], /) -> bool: ...

            """Serialize the event into ZPP bytes for pickling."""

            """Rehydrate the event from pickled ZPP bytes."""

symusic\.core\.Tempo$:
    class Tempo(Generic[TimeUnitT]):
        """
        Tempo[TimeUnitT](time: float, mspq: int)
        Tempo change stored as microseconds-per-quarter note at a second timestamp. The ``qpm`` property mirrors beats-per-minute and mutating it updates ``mspq`` accordingly.
        - Time values are 32-bit floats measured in seconds.
        - Optimized for audio alignment, wall-clock automation, or duration-based editing
        """
        @overload
        def __init__(self, other: Tempo[TimeUnitT], /) -> None:
            """Copy an existing event into this shared pointer wrapper."""
        @overload
        def __init__(self, time: float, qpm: float | None = None, mspq: int | None = None) -> None:
            """
